title: Number theory in Sage
intro: Sage's number theory, in the reader's browser: primes, factorizations, congruences, arithmetic functions, class numbers and an elliptic curve. Each code item is Sage code; its output shows under it.

nodes.title: Number theory
nodes.text: The integers, and what lies over them.

nodes.title: Fermat's $F_5$ is not prime
nodes.text: Fermat thought every $F_n = 2^{2^n} + 1$ prime; Euler found the factor $641$ of $F_5$ in 1732.

nodes.title: Arithmetic functions
nodes.code: [(n, euler_phi(n), sigma(n), moebius(n)) for n in [12, 28, 30]]

nodes.title: Class numbers
nodes.text: Of $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-d})$: for squarefree $d > 0$, the class number is $1$ for exactly nine $d$, the nine imaginary quadratic fields of class number $1$ (Heegner, Baker, Stark).

nodes.title: An elliptic curve
nodes.text: $y^2 + y = x^3 - x$, of conductor $37$: the first curve of rank $1$.

nodes.title: Twin primes among them
nodes.code: [(p, p + 2) for p in P if is_prime(p + 2)]

steps.say: `P` is defined in one item and read in another: the board runs them in order, and reruns the reader when `P` changes.
Sage factors exactly, with arbitrary-size integers.
